# Triad batch evaluation summary

Generated by `scripts/batch_eval_report.py`. Rows sampled with seed 2026 from `datasets/flights.csv` (stratified: half WEATHER_DELAY>15 -> AIRBORNE, half LATE_AIRCRAFT_DELAY>20 & WEATHER_DELAY<=15 -> GROUND); the 20 LLM rows are a subset of the 200 stub rows. Scenario seed 0.

**Synthetic data:** flight identity, route, schedule and delay minutes are real (US DOT 2015). Everything the agents negotiate over is SYNTHETIC, generated by `triad.data.enrich` from `config/*.yaml`: arrival slots/runways, gates, fuel, crew duty, connections, next leg, MEL defects, NOTAM/weather text, and the EUR cost weights (`config/costs.yaml`). All costs below are model costs, not airline figures.

**Cost yardstick:** every cost is recomputed with the stub agents' `cost_eur` (ground-truth private data), the same function the fallback solver uses, so stub, LLM and baselines are on one scale. `hard_violations_recheck` re-runs shared + all three stub checkers on the committed plan, independent of what the (possibly LLM) agents believed.

**Baselines:** *fallback* = project solver (`--ai-off`), cheapest option passing all hard checks. *FCFS (status quo, SIMULATED)* = earliest-arrival generator option that keeps the originally planned gate, is not a diversion, uses no counter-proposal, and passes every hard check. *FCFS-any* = `triad.baseline.fcfs_resolution` (earliest safe arrival, any gate). Negative = cheaper than baseline.

> The *vs fallback* comparison is not expected to be negative: the fallback already picks the cheapest safe option among generated options, so negotiation can at best match it (or beat it only through a validated counter-proposal). Its value is showing how much cost the negotiated consensus gives up, in exchange for agent buy-in.
